Season.title: Training block
Season.label: {phase} · week {week} of {weeks}

explain.base: Base phase: lots of easy endurance and technique, at most one tempo session. This is your foundation.
explain.build: Build phase: the volume grows and threshold sessions come in. Every block a little harder.
explain.peak: Peak phase: your hardest weeks, with sessions at race pace. After this you freshen up for the race.
explain.maintain: You train in blocks of building and recovery to stay fit. Set a goal for a real build-up.
explain.recovery: Recovery week: less volume and no hard sessions. This is when your body gets stronger from the last weeks' work.
explain.taper: Taper: much less volume, with a few short sharp efforts, so you arrive fresh and sharp at the start.
explain.race: Race week: short and easy, a few short accelerations to stay sharp. Good luck!

Season.undoRecovery: Not a recovery week after all

problem.title: Most training plans assume a 9-to-5. Your life doesn't.
problem.body: Night shifts, late meetings, a week with only two free evenings. A fixed plan breaks, you skip sessions, and you feel like you're falling behind.

steps.title: 3 steps. Then it keeps up with you.

one.title: Tell us your week
one.body: Which days you can train, and for how long. Fixed hours, variable or shifts: all fine.

two.title: Your coach team plans it
two.body: A head coach plus run, bike and swim specialists build your week, from base to race day.

three.title: Life changes? So does your plan
three.body: Drag a session to another day, or ask your coach for a proposal. You approve the change.

features.title: Everything your week needs. Nothing it doesn't.

app.body: See every session, move what doesn't fit, and talk to your coach. Built for your phone, from the first day.
app.imageAlt: The Runvex app on an iPhone, showing today's training and the week's progress

story.quote: I train for triathlon next to a job that never has the same week twice. I couldn't find a plan that kept up, so I built one.
story.author: Jeremy, founder of Runvex

cta.title: Be first in line
cta.body: Join the waitlist and get early access when Runvex launches on the App Store.

launch.a: We're building and testing right now. Join the waitlist and you'll be the first to know: one email when Runvex launches on the App Store, nothing else.

price.a: We’ll share pricing on this website before launch. Joining the waitlist is free and comes with no commitment.

watches.a: Any watch that exports .FIT files, like Garmin, Coros, Suunto and Wahoo. Upload your activity and your coach takes it into account. Direct sync is on our roadmap.

data.a: Yes. Your data is stored in the EU. Heart rate data is only saved with your permission and is never sent to AI. Your name, email and date of birth are never shared with the AI coach either.

goal.q: Do I need a race goal?
goal.a: No. With a race, your plan builds towards race day: base, build, peak and taper. Without one, Runvex keeps you fit with a steady rhythm of training and recovery weeks.

missed.q: What happens if I miss a session?
missed.a: Nothing breaks. Drag it to another day, or ask your coach to adjust your week. If life gets busy, your coach can turn it into a recovery week.

example.eyebrow: Your shifts change. Your training follows.
example.title: An unexpected night shift on Thursday?
example.body: You don’t have to rebuild your plan yourself. Ask your coach to adjust your week around the time you do have.
example.label: Example
example.proposal: “Let’s skip the tempo session this week and keep Saturday shorter and easy. That leaves room to recover after your night shift.”
example.approval: A proposal, not an automatic change. You decide what fits.
